fixes.explanation: Reuben is a fair guess, baker. His name opens the list of Jacob's sons as Jacob's firstborn (Genesis 46:8). But the text says Jacob sent Judah ahead to Joseph to get directions to Goshen (Genesis 46:28). Judah is the one who goes out front. Reuben is a good pick, just not for this errand.

Benjamin, Joseph's brother, and both of them were born to Rachel (Genesis 46:19). I see the pull, since a brother heading to a brother feels right. But verse 28 says Jacob sent Judah ahead to Joseph to get directions to Goshen. Judah is the one who goes first.

Yes, baker. Joseph prepared his chariot and went to meet his father, and then the text says he presented himself to him, embraced him, and wept profusely (Genesis 46:29). So he doesn't greet his father from up high. He holds him and cries hard. Jacob once believed Joseph was gone (Genesis 37:33–35), so I think this hug carries a whole lot of feeling.

That's right, friend. Joseph brings in his father Jacob and presents him before Pharaoh, Egypt's king, and Jacob blesses him (Genesis 47:7). Then verse 10 says Jacob blessed Pharaoh again as he departed. So Jacob blesses him at both ends of the visit. That's a good way to walk into a room and a good way to walk out.

175 is a real number in Genesis. It's how long Abraham lived (Genesis 25:7), and Abraham was Jacob's grandfather, since Isaac was Abraham's son and Jacob was Isaac's son (Genesis 25:19, 26). But here Jacob says, “My travels have lasted 130 years…” That's his own number, and it's lower. Same family, different road.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The passage does not say that Reuben stays with the wagons.
The passage does not say that Benjamin rides with the family or that the others are still loading wagons when Judah goes ahead.
Jacob's earlier belief that Joseph was gone is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference, such as Genesis 37:33–35.
Genesis 25:7 supports Abraham's age, but not the statement that he was Jacob's grandfather. That relationship also needs a reference, such as Genesis 25:19, 26.
